jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoctoral Researcher on CO2 Solid Adsorbent Shaping and Degradation

The Laboratory for Building Energy Materials and Components develops advanced and/or low eco-impact, porous materials for insulation, sorption, and energy-related applications. Our research portfolio spans fundamental materials chemistry, process–structure–property relationships, and application-driven R&D, in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners.

To strengthen our team, we are seeking a highly motivated researcher with a strong background in solid adsorbents/gas adsorption/separation.

Project Focus
 The project builds on Empa’s expertise in the field of sorbents and carbon capture. The position is part of the National Center of Competence in Research (NCCR) "Separations", a collaborative project lead by EPFL (Prof. Wendy Queen) and further involving ETH Zurich, University of Fribourg, HES-SO, Northwestern University (USA) and University of Alberta (Canada).

The NCCR focuses on three key challenges:

• CO2 capture from air: Developing scalable, cost-effective processes to efficiently remove atmospheric CO2.

• High-temperature ammonia separation: Creating novel high temperature separation technologies to make ammonia synthesis significantly more energy-efficient.

• Recovery of critical metals: Developing processes to recover valuable metals such as lithium and cobalt from waste streams, enabling secure and sustainable material cycles.

Your tasks

As part of the NCCR-Network, you will contribute to the project aims in the areas of shaped CO2 adsorbents and sorbent ageing. Within the framework of the NCCR project with well-defined objectives, you will be encouraged to develop independent ideas, propose new concepts, and test them experimentally and/or computationally. The role is ideally suited to strengthen your pre-existing expertise and enhance your academic track record.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Help coordinate project activities and develop synergies within the team and between project partners.

• Supervise intern students contributing to the project.

• Elucidate chemical as well as structural ageing mechanisms of structured and pure solid sorbents under different ageing conditions.

• Develop accelerated and high throughput sorbent ageing protocols.

• Help define mitigation strategies for sorbent ageing.

• Develop versatile, upscalable sorbent shaping/coating procedures.

• Help shape new, emerging scientific research lines within the project scope and publish/communicate your scientific results

Your profile

• A high level of curiosity, independence, teamwork skills and motivation

• Doctoral degree or equivalent research experience in porous materials, surface or adsorption/separation science or a closely related field

• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English

Experience or familiarity with one of the following topics:

• Characterization of sorbent/porous materials characterization e.g. nitrogen sorption (BET, BJH, NLDFT), breakthrough measurements, SEM, TEM, TGA, FTIR, NMR, thermal conductivity measurements

• Synthesis and/or shaping of solid sorbents.

• Sorbent modelling and prediction of performance or ageing.

Our offer

We offer a stimulating, international, and collaborative research environment at a leading research institution with state-of-the-art infrastructure. The laboratory and supervisors provide a supportive and safe-to-fail work environment. As part of the ETH Domain, we offer attractive employment conditions and excellent opportunities for professional and personal development. Start date is upon agreement for a duration of 2 years.

We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

Il nostro portafoglio di ricerca abbraccia la chimica dei materiali fondamentali, le relazioni struttura-proprietà e R&D, in stretta collaborazione con partner accademici e industriali. Per rafforzare il nostro team, stiamo cercando un ricercatore altamente motivato con uno sfondo forte in adsorbents solidi / gas adsorbimento / separazione. La posizione è parte del National Center of Competence in Research (NCCR) "Separations", un progetto collaborativo guidato da EPFL (Prof. Wendy Queen) e coinvolge ulteriormente ETH Zurich, University of Fribourg, HES-SO, Northwestern University (USA) e University of Alberta (Canada). • CO2 cattura dall'aria: sviluppo di processi scalabili e convenienti per rimuovere efficacemente la CO2 atmosferica.
• Separazione dell'ammoniaca ad alta temperatura: creazione di nuove tecnologie di separazione ad alta temperatura per rendere la sintesi dell'ammoniaca significativamente più efficiente.
• Recupero dei metalli critici: sviluppo di processi per recuperare metalli preziosi come litio e cobalto dai flussi di rifiuti, consentendo cicli materiali sicuri e sostenibili. Il ruolo è ideale per rafforzare la vostra esperienza preesistente e migliorare il vostro record di traccia accademica. Le tue responsabilità includono:
• Aiuta a coordinare le attività di progetto e sviluppare sinergie all'interno del team e tra i partner di progetto.
• Supervise studenti tirocinanti che contribuiscono al progetto.
• Elucidi i meccanismi di invecchiamento chimico e strutturale di sorbenti solidi strutturati e puri in diverse condizioni di invecchiamento.
• Sviluppare protocolli di invecchiamento sorbenti accelerati e ad alto rendimento.
• Aiuta a definire strategie di mitigazione per l'invecchiamento sorbente.
• Sviluppare procedure di modellazione/coating sorbent versatili e scalabili.
• Aiuta a modellare nuove linee di ricerca scientifiche emergenti nell'ambito del progetto e pubblicare/comunicare i risultati scientifici Il tuo profilo
• Un alto livello di curiosità, indipendenza, abilità di lavoro di squadra e motivazione
• Grado medico o esperienza di ricerca equivalente in materiali porosi, superficie o adsorbimento/separazione scienza o un campo strettamente correlato
• Eccellente capacità di comunicazione scritta e orale in inglese Esperienza o familiarità con uno dei seguenti argomenti:
• Caratterizzazione di materiali sorbenti/porosi caratterizzazione come ad esempio l'assorbimento di azoto (BET, BJH, NLDFT), misurazioni innovative, SEM, TEM, TGA, FTIR, NMR, misurazioni di conducibilità termica
• Sintesi e/o sagomatura di solidi sorbenti.
• Modellazione sorbente e previsione delle prestazioni o dell'invecchiamento. La nostra offerta Offriamo un ambiente di ricerca stimolante, internazionale e collaborativo in un istituto di ricerca leader con infrastrutture all'avanguardia. Il laboratorio e i supervisori forniscono un ambiente di lavoro solidale e sicuro. Come parte del Dominio ETH, offriamo condizioni di lavoro attraenti e ottime opportunità per lo sviluppo professionale e personale. La data di inizio è su accordo per una durata di 2 anni. Viviamo una cultura di inclusione e rispetto. Diamo il benvenuto a tutte le persone che sono interessate a attività innovative, sostenibili e significative - questo è ciò che conta. Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la tua candidatura online completa, tra cui una lettera di motivazione, CV, certificati, diplomi e dettagli di contatto di due persone di riferimento. Si prega di inviare questi esclusivamente tramite il nostro portale di lavoro. Le domande per e-mail e per posta non saranno considerate.

Die Empa ist eine Forschungseinrichtung des ETH-Bereichs. Postdoktorandin zum Thema CO2 Solid Adsorbent Shaping and Degradation Das Laboratory for Building Energy Materials and Components entwickelt fortschrittliche und/oder umweltfreundliche, poröse Materialien für Isolations-, Sorptions- und energiebezogene Anwendungen. Unser Forschungsportfolio umfasst grundlegende Materialchemie, Prozess-Struktur-Eigenschaftsbeziehungen und anwendungsorientierte Forschung und Entwicklung in enger Zusammenarbeit mit akademischen und industriellen Partnern. Um unser Team zu stärken, suchen wir einen hochmotivierten Forscher mit einem starken Hintergrund in festen Adsorbentien / Gasadsorption / Trennung. Projektschwerpunkt Das Projekt baut auf der Expertise der Empa im Bereich Sorbentien und Kohlenstoffabscheidung auf. Die Position ist Teil des National Center of Competence in Research (NCCR) "Separations", einem Verbundprojekt unter der Leitung der EPFL (Prof. Wendy Queen) und weiter unter Beteiligung der ETH Zürich, Universität Freiburg, HES-SO, Northwestern University (USA) und University of Alberta (Kanada). Der NFS konzentriert sich auf drei zentrale Herausforderungen:
• CO2-Abscheidung aus der Luft: Entwicklung skalierbarer, kostengünstiger Prozesse zur effizienten Entfernung von atmosphärischem CO2.
• Hochtemperatur-Ammoniak-Trennung: Entwicklung neuartiger Hochtemperatur-Trenntechnologien, um die Ammoniaksynthese deutlich energieeffizienter zu gestalten.
• Rückgewinnung kritischer Metalle: Entwicklung von Prozessen zur Rückgewinnung wertvoller Metalle wie Lithium und Kobalt aus Abfallströmen, die sichere und nachhaltige Stoffkreisläufe ermöglichen. Ihre Aufgaben Im Rahmen des NFS-Netzwerks tragen Sie zu den Projektzielen in den Bereichen geformte CO2-Adsorbentien und Sorbensalterung bei. Die Rolle ist ideal geeignet, um Ihre bereits bestehende Expertise zu stärken und Ihre akademische Erfolgsbilanz zu verbessern. Ihre Aufgaben umfassen:

• Beaufsichtigen Sie Praktikanten, die zum Projekt beitragen.
• Chemische sowie strukturelle Alterungsmechanismen von strukturierten und reinen festen Sorbentien unter verschiedenen Alterungsbedingungen aufklären.
• Entwicklung beschleunigter und hochdurchsatzfähiger Sorbensalterungsprotokolle.
• Helfen Sie bei der Definition von Minderungsstrategien für das Altern von Sorbenten.
• Entwicklung vielseitiger, hochskalierbarer Verfahren zur Formgebung/Beschichtung von Sorbentien.
• Helfen Sie, neue, aufkommende wissenschaftliche Forschungslinien innerhalb des Projektumfangs zu gestalten und veröffentlichen / kommunizieren Sie Ihre wissenschaftlichen Ergebnisse Dein Profil

• Promotion oder gleichwertige Forschungserfahrung in porösen Materialien, Oberflächen- oder Adsorptions-/Trennungswissenschaften oder einem eng verwandten Gebiet
• Hervorragende schriftliche und mündliche Kommunikationsfähigkeiten in Englisch Erfahrung oder Vertrautheit mit einem der folgenden Themen:
• Charakterisierung von Sorbens/porösen Materialien, z. B. Stickstoffsorption (BET, BJH, NLDFT), Durchbruchsmessungen, SEM, TEM, TGA, FTIR, NMR, Wärmeleitfähigkeitsmessungen

Bitte senden Sie diese ausschließlich über unser Jobportal. Bewerbungen per E-Mail und Post werden nicht berücksichtigt.
descriptionByLocale.fr:
La science et la technologie des matériaux sont notre passion. Grâce à nos recherches de pointe, les quelque 1 100 employés d'Empa apportent une contribution essentielle au bien-être de la société pour un avenir digne d'être vécu. Empa est une institution de recherche du domaine ETH. Chercheur postdoctoral sur la formation et la dégradation des adsorbants solides de CO2 Le Laboratoire des matériaux et composants énergétiques du bâtiment développe des matériaux d'isolation, de sorption et d'utilisation liés à l'énergie, de pointe ou à faible impact environnemental. Notre portefeuille de recherche couvre la chimie fondamentale des matériaux, les relations entre les processus et la propriété et la R-D axée sur les applications, en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires et industriels. Pour renforcer notre équipe, nous recherchons un chercheur hautement motivé ayant une solide expérience en adsorbants solides/adsorption/séparation de gaz. Objectif du projet Le projet s'appuie sur l'expertise d'Empa dans le domaine des sorbants et du captage du carbone. Ce poste fait partie du National Center of Competence in Research (NCCR) "Separations", un projet collaboratif dirigé par l'EPFL (Prof. Wendy Queen) et auquel participent également l'ETH Zurich, l'Université de Fribourg, HES-SO, l'Université du Nord-Ouest (USA) et l'Université de l'Alberta (Canada). Le CCNR se concentre sur trois défis clés :
• Capture de CO2 dans l'air : Mettre au point des processus évolutifs et rentables pour éliminer efficacement le CO2 atmosphérique.
• Séparation à haute température de l'ammoniac: Création de nouvelles technologies de séparation à haute température pour rendre la synthèse de l'ammoniac significativement plus économe en énergie.
• Récupération des métaux essentiels : Mettre au point des processus pour récupérer des métaux précieux tels que le lithium et le cobalt dans les flux de déchets, permettant des cycles de matières sûrs et durables. Vos tâches Dans le cadre du réseau NCCR, vous contribuerez aux objectifs du projet dans les domaines des adsorbants en forme de CO2 et du vieillissement sorbant. Dans le cadre du projet du CCNR avec des objectifs bien définis, vous serez encouragé à développer des idées indépendantes, à proposer de nouveaux concepts et à les tester expérimentalement et/ou par calcul. Le rôle est idéal pour renforcer votre expertise préexistante et améliorer votre expérience académique. Vos responsabilités comprendront :
• Aider à coordonner les activités du projet et à développer des synergies au sein de l'équipe et entre les partenaires du projet.
• Superviser les étudiants stagiaires qui contribuent au projet.
• Élucidate chimique ainsi que les mécanismes de vieillissement structurel des sorbants solides structurés et purs dans différentes conditions de vieillissement.
• Élaborer des protocoles de vieillissement sorbant à débit accéléré et élevé.
• Aider à définir des stratégies d'atténuation du vieillissement sorbant.
• Développer des procédures polyvalentes et évolutives de façonnage et de revêtement des sorbants.
• Aider à façonner les nouvelles lignes de recherche scientifique dans le cadre du projet et publier/communiquer vos résultats scientifiques Votre profil
• Un haut niveau de curiosité, d'indépendance, d'esprit d'équipe et de motivation
• Diplôme de doctorat ou expérience de recherche équivalente en matériaux poreux, en sciences de surface ou d'adsorption/séparation ou dans un domaine étroitement lié
• Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais Expérience ou connaissance de l'un des sujets suivants :
• Caractérisation de la caractérisation des matériaux sorbants/poreux, p.ex. sorption d'azote (BET, BJH, NLDFT), mesures de rupture, SEM, TEM, TGA, FTIR, RMN, mesures de conductivité thermique
• Synthèse et/ou mise en forme des sorbants solides.
• Modélisation et prédiction des performances ou du vieillissement. Notre offre Nous offrons un environnement de recherche stimulant, international et collaboratif dans un établissement de recherche de premier plan doté d'une infrastructure de pointe. Le laboratoire et les superviseurs offrent un milieu de travail favorable et sécuritaire. Dans le domaine de l'ETH, nous offrons des conditions d'emploi attrayantes et d'excellentes possibilités de développement professionnel et personnel. La date de début est convenue pour une durée de 2 ans. Nous vivons une culture d'inclusion et de respect. Nous accueillons toutes les personnes qui s'intéressent à des activités novatrices, durables et significatives - c'est ce qui compte. Nous sommes impatients de recevoir votre candidature en ligne complète comprenant une lettre de motivation, CV, certificats, diplômes et coordonnées de deux personnes de référence. Veuillez les soumettre exclusivement via notre portail d'emploi. Les demandes par courrier électronique et par la poste ne seront pas prises en considération.

jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoc position in CO2 electrocatalysis under realistic conditions

Empa’s Laboratory Materials for Energy Conversion focuses on materials and device innovation for sustainable energy conversion and storage technologies.

Your tasks

The research project focuses on understanding the electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into sustainable products. Your task will include:

• Assemble and validate modular electrocatalytic reactors and analysis methods for realistic CO2 electrocatalysis, with a focus on parallel investigations and accelerated aging.

• Dissect degradation processes of CO2 electroreduction catalyst, electrodes, and ionomer membranes under diverse real-world operating conditions, using operando electrochemical and spectroscopic methods.

• Lead synchrotron campaigns aiming at unveiling the degradation mechanism of catalysts, electrodes, and ionomer membranes with high time resolution, operando x-ray measurements.

• Develop electrode architecture and catalyst/electrode modification strategies for enhanced durability, using different fabrication methods.

This postdoc position is part of an international collaborative project involving several academic and industrial partners.

Your profile

We are looking for a highly motivated team player who thrives in a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment. The ideal candidate possesses a PhD degree in chemistry or chemical engineering, materials science, physics, or related discipline. As this project is a cutting-edge research activity beyond the current state-of-the-art in electrocatalysis, we are looking for someone creative, curious, highly motivated, and with excellent problem-solving and technical skills. Prior experience in electrochemistry and/or catalysis is a strong advantage. The successful candidate will be expected to work independently in the lab while collaborating and communicating effectively with our multidisciplinary team.

Our offer

You will join a dynamic young international research group working in a brand new laboratory building located at Empa’s campus in Dübendorf near downtown Zürich. In addition to our state-of-the-art electrocatalysis facilities encompassing catalyst and electrode synthesis, parallel electrochemical characterizations and comprehensive gas and liquid analytics, the lab owns and operates a large array of instruments including X-ray diffractometers, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, infrared and Raman spectrometers, and argon ion mills and electron microscopes. The position is closely connected to two national research initiatives focusing on the synthesis of sustainable fuels and chemicals providing many opportunities to interact with a large and high-profile network that includes members of both academia and industry.

Empa is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We strongly encourage applications from female researchers and individuals from underrepresented backgrounds. We believe diversity drives innovation and scientific excellence. Join us in contributing to groundbreaking research in sustainable energy technologies!

We look forward to receiving your online application including a two-page motivation letter, CV, scholarly records, diplomas with transcripts, and at least two reference letters. Only complete applications will be considered. Please upload all documents through our webpage, applications via E-mail cannot be accepted.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoc position in CO2 electrocatalysis under realistic conditions

Empa’s Laboratory Materials for Energy Conversion focuses on materials and device innovation for sustainable energy conversion and storage technologies.

Your tasks

The research project focuses on understanding the electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into sustainable products. Your task will include:

• Assemble and validate modular electrocatalytic reactors and analysis methods for realistic CO2 electrocatalysis, with a focus on parallel investigations and accelerated aging.

• Dissect degradation processes of CO2 electroreduction catalyst, electrodes, and ionomer membranes under diverse real-world operating conditions, using operando electrochemical and spectroscopic methods.

• Lead synchrotron campaigns aiming at unveiling the degradation mechanism of catalysts, electrodes, and ionomer membranes with high time resolution, operando x-ray measurements.

• Develop electrode architecture and catalyst/electrode modification strategies for enhanced durability, using different fabrication methods.

This postdoc position is part of an international collaborative project involving several academic and industrial partners.

Your profile

We are looking for a highly motivated team player who thrives in a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment. The ideal candidate possesses a PhD degree in chemistry or chemical engineering, materials science, physics, or related discipline. As this project is a cutting-edge research activity beyond the current state-of-the-art in electrocatalysis, we are looking for someone creative, curious, highly motivated, and with excellent problem-solving and technical skills. Prior experience in electrochemistry and/or catalysis is a strong advantage. The successful candidate will be expected to work independently in the lab while collaborating and communicating effectively with our multidisciplinary team.

Our offer

You will join a dynamic young international research group working in a brand new laboratory building located at Empa’s campus in Dübendorf near downtown Zürich. In addition to our state-of-the-art electrocatalysis facilities encompassing catalyst and electrode synthesis, parallel electrochemical characterizations and comprehensive gas and liquid analytics, the lab owns and operates a large array of instruments including X-ray diffractometers, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, infrared and Raman spectrometers, and argon ion mills and electron microscopes. The position is closely connected to two national research initiatives focusing on the synthesis of sustainable fuels and chemicals providing many opportunities to interact with a large and high-profile network that includes members of both academia and industry.

Empa is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We strongly encourage applications from female researchers and individuals from underrepresented backgrounds. We believe diversity drives innovation and scientific excellence. Join us in contributing to groundbreaking research in sustainable energy technologies!

We look forward to receiving your online application including a two-page motivation letter, CV, scholarly records, diplomas with transcripts, and at least two reference letters. Only complete applications will be considered. Please upload all documents through our webpage, applications via E-mail cannot be accepted.

La science et la technologie des matériaux sont notre passion. Grâce à nos recherches de pointe, les quelque 1 100 employés d'Empa apportent une contribution essentielle au bien-être de la société pour un avenir digne d'être vécu. Empa est une institution de recherche du domaine ETH. Position postdoc dans l'électrocatalyse CO2 dans des conditions réalistes Les matériaux de laboratoire pour la conversion de l'énergie sont axés sur l'innovation des matériaux et des appareils pour des technologies de conversion et de stockage durables de l'énergie. Vos tâches Le projet de recherche vise à comprendre la conversion électrocatalytique du CO2 en produits durables. Votre tâche comprendra :
• Assembler et valider des réacteurs électrocatalytiques modulaires et des méthodes d'analyse pour l'électrocatalyse réaliste du CO2, en mettant l'accent sur les enquêtes parallèles et le vieillissement accéléré.
• Disséquer les processus de dégradation du catalyseur d'électroréduction du CO2, des électrodes et des membranes d'ionomères dans diverses conditions d'exploitation réelles, en utilisant des méthodes électrochimiques et spectroscopiques.
• Campagnes de synchrotrons de plomb visant à dévoiler le mécanisme de dégradation des catalyseurs, des électrodes et des membranes ionomères à haute résolution temporelle, mesures par rayons X d'opérando.
• Développer l'architecture des électrodes et des stratégies de modification des catalyseurs/électrodes pour une durabilité accrue, en utilisant différentes méthodes de fabrication. Ce poste postdoc fait partie d'un projet de collaboration internationale impliquant plusieurs partenaires académiques et industriels. Votre profil Nous cherchons un joueur d'équipe hautement motivé qui prospère dans un environnement de recherche collaboratif et interdisciplinaire. Le candidat idéal possède un doctorat en chimie ou en génie chimique, sciences des matériaux, physique ou discipline connexe. Comme ce projet est une activité de recherche de pointe au-delà de l'état actuel de l'électrocatalyse, nous sommes à la recherche de quelqu'un de créatif, curieux, très motivé, et avec d'excellentes compétences techniques et de résolution de problèmes. L'expérience antérieure en électrochimie et/ou en catalyse est un avantage important. On s'attend à ce que le candidat reçu travaille de façon indépendante au laboratoire tout en collaborant et en communiquant efficacement avec notre équipe multidisciplinaire. Notre offre Vous rejoindrez un jeune groupe de recherche international dynamique travaillant dans un tout nouveau bâtiment de laboratoire situé sur le campus d'Empa, à Dübendorf, près du centre-ville de Zürich. En plus de nos installations d'électrocatalyse de pointe comprenant la synthèse des catalyseurs et des électrodes, les caractérisations électrochimiques parallèles et l'analyse complète des gaz et des liquides, le laboratoire possède et exploite une vaste gamme d'instruments, dont les diffractomètres à rayons X, la spectroscopie par photoélectrons à rayons X, les spectromètres infrarouges et Raman, ainsi que les argon-ions et les microscopes électroniques. La position est étroitement liée à deux initiatives nationales de recherche axées sur la synthèse de combustibles et de produits chimiques durables, offrant de nombreuses possibilités d'interagir avec un réseau de grande envergure qui comprend des membres du milieu universitaire et de l'industrie. Empa est attachée à la diversité, à l'équité et à l'inclusion. Nous encourageons vivement les candidatures de femmes chercheurs et de personnes issues de milieux sous-représentés. jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoc in applied laser physics

The Laboratory of Advanced Materials Processing (LAMP) is a multidisciplinary research unit that develops innovative functional modification of materials by beam (e.g. laser light, electrons) and plasma induced processing. LAMP provides full cycle technology development, starting from novel materials, deep understanding of the background physics of beam-matter interactions, development of automated AI/ML systems for novel materials processing and quality insurance. The lab combines additive manufacturing, large scale laser micro-processing, multiscale modelling and AI/ML for the quality monitoring/control, at the end offering to the society novel nanostructured materials, their shape-forming and integration into devices.

Your tasks

• Operation of different laser platforms

• Conceptualization and setup of optical systems

• Hardware synchronization and data acquisition

• Conduction of experimental campaigns, evaluation of results and reporting

Your profile

• PhD degree in Physics/Photonics/Engineering or equivalent

• Experience: Laser applications (measuring, processing, etc.), optical system design, assembly and usage

• Skills: Hands-on experimental mindset, strong understanding of laser and optical physics, strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, experience with data analysis and experimental optimization

• English, French and German as a plus

Our offer

Empa offers a dynamic and inspiring research environment at its Thun campus, located near Bern. You will work on a scientifically and technologically cutting-edge topic of high relevance and novelty, with direct access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure and equipment. As part of an experienced and multidisciplinary project team with strong national and international collaborations, you will receive full support in advancing the current project as well as in shaping and realizing your own scientific ideas within the lab's research activities. You will be encouraged and supported in producing high-impact results, publishing in leading international peer-reviewed journals, and pursuing your personal and professional development. The position is available with a starting date in September 2026 and a duration of one year with the possibility of extension.

We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoc/Engineer in acoustics for laser processing (80-100%)

The Laboratory of Advanced Materials Processing (LAMP) is a multidisciplinary research unit that develops innovative functional modification of materials by beam (e.g. laser light, electrons) and plasma induced processing. LAMP provides full cycle technology development, starting from novel materials, deep understanding of the background physics of beam-matter interactions, development of automated AI/ML systems for novel materials processing and quality insurance. The lab combines additive manufacturing, large scale laser micro-processing, multiscale modelling and AI/ML for the quality monitoring/control, at the end offering to the society novel nanostructured materials, their shape-forming and integration into devices.

Your tasks

• R&D of acoustic system (acoustics/multi-physics simulation, experimental planning, setup, measurements, analysis)

• Conceptualization and realization of novel setups (hardware integration, CAD design, assembly, etc.)

• Software development (data acquisition and processing, system communication)

Your profile

• FH/University degree (Master or PhD) Acoustics/Electronics/Engineering or equivalent

• Experience: Acoustics (active, passive), laser processing

• Skills: R&D manufacturing, software development (machine communication, data acquisition, etc.), hardware integration

• English, French and German as a plus

Our offer

Empa offers a dynamic and inspiring research environment at its Thun campus, located near Bern. You will work on a scientifically and technologically cutting-edge topic of high relevance and novelty, with direct access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure and equipment. As part of an experienced and multidisciplinary project team with strong national and international collaborations, you will receive full support in advancing the current project as well as in shaping and realizing your own scientific ideas within the lab's research activities. You will be encouraged and supported in producing high-impact results, publishing in leading international peer-reviewed journals, and pursuing your personal and professional development. The position is available with a starting date in September 2026 and a duration of one year with the possibility of extension.

We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

PostDoc position in 3D X-ray histopathology of colorectal tumors

Empa’s Centre for X-ray Analytics develops X-ray analytical and imaging methods for understanding materials structure in material, life- and medical sciences.

The PostDoc research will be part of a multi-center research project on applying and combining multi-modal 2D and 3D imaging methods for understanding metastasis and tumor deposit formation in colorectal tumors. Specifically, the work will focus on optimizing 3D X-ray virtual histology methods by phase-contrast micro-CT and corresponding image processing techniques also with view on combining it with other 2D and 3D techniques such as H&E and LSFM. The work will be done in close cooperation and synergy with an already running PhD project. Partly existing database will be used and extended to develop image processing pipelines and models for the automated evaluation of 3D data sets towards answering clinical research questions. The project is highly interdisciplinary and is carried out in close collaboration with imaging, image analysis and clinical experts from Switzerland and abroad. Involvement in other closely related research activities of the imaging group at the X-ray Center is also foreseen.

Your contribution

• Application and further development of 3D digital histopathology by X-ray phase contrast micro-CT

• Development of image processing and ML tools and models for the automated identification and quantification of clinically relevant morphological features in metastatic colorectal tumors and lymph nodes

• Data management, data treatment

Your profile

If you would like to make a major impact on 3D X-ray based digital pathology and corresponding image processing methods, you are highly motivated, a team player, communicative and passionate working in an interdisciplinary field and fulfill the following criteria:
• Completed PhD in X-ray imaging or in a field very closely related

• Have a very solid background in the technical and theoretical details of X-ray imaging and in phase contrast techniques

• Have very good lab skills

• Have preferably experience in the biomedical domain and in image processing

• Have preferably experience using ML models and tools (e.g. radiomics) in image processing and very good skills in programming

• Fluent in English, (German is beneficial)
 then, this position might be for you.

Our offer

Project duration is two years. The candidate will perform his/her research at Empa in Dübendorf. Desired starting date is as soon as reasonably possible or upon mutual agreement.

We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

PhD Position on All-Solid-State Batteries

Empa’s Laboratory Materials for Energy Conversion focuses on materials and device innovation for sustainable energy technologies.

Your tasks

The aim of this PhD project is to investigate lithium- and sodium-based solid-state batteries using muon-based bulk and interface characterization techniques. The main objective is to gain a mechanistic understanding of electrochemical performance, with a focus on ion distribution, transport, and degradation processes during battery operation.
 The project addresses key questions such as the formation of Li/Na concentration gradients during charge and discharge, the evolution of interphases, and degradation mechanisms including ageing, material dissolution (leaching), and transition-metal migration. Muon-based methods will be used to probe depth-resolved properties that are difficult to access with conventional techniques, enabling new insights into buried interfaces and bulk transport phenomena.

Your work will focus on electrochemical and structural characterization of battery materials and cells, combined with muon-based experiments. You will design and carry out experiments to identify reaction pathways and degradation mechanisms, and analyze complex datasets to connect microscopic processes with macroscopic performance. Close collaboration with project partners will support the development and testing of materials and cell concepts.

Your profile

You hold a Master’s degree in chemistry, materials science, or a related field, experience in electrochemistry or batteries is an advantage. Excellent English skills are required.

Our offer

You will conduct your research in Empa’s laboratories in Dübendorf and will be enrolled in the doctoral program in Electrical Engineering at ETH Zurich. The project is part of the National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Muoniverse and is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation.
 Muoniverse connects over 30 research groups and offers a structured research school with training, exchange opportunities, and career development. We are looking for candidates who enjoy collaborative, interdisciplinary research and value openness and shared progress. Muoniverse is committed to equal opportunities, diversity, and an inclusive research culture.

You will independently conduct experiments, including muon beamline studies, collaborate with academic and industrial partners, and disseminate your results through publications and presentations. Our laboratories provide access to a broad range of battery research infrastructure, including gloveboxes, furnaces, spectroscopy, microscopy, and extensive electrochemical testing facilities.

Start date is October 1st, 2026 or upon agreement.

Empa is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We strongly encourage applications from female researchers and individuals from underrepresented backgrounds. We believe diversity drives innovation and scientific excellence. Join us in contributing to groundbreaking research in sustainable energy technologies!

We look forward to receiving your online application including a two-page motivation letter, CV, scholarly records, diplomas with transcripts, and at least two reference letters. Only complete applications will be considered. Please upload all documents through our webpage, applications via E-mail cannot be accepted.

descriptionByLocale.it:
La scienza dei materiali e la tecnologia sono la nostra passione. Con la nostra ricerca all'avanguardia, i circa 1.100 dipendenti di Empa danno un contributo essenziale al benessere della società per un futuro che vale la pena di vivere. Empa è un'istituzione di ricerca del dominio ETH. PhD Position sulle batterie All-Solid-State I materiali di laboratorio di Empa per la conversione dell’energia si concentrano sull’innovazione dei materiali e dei dispositivi per le tecnologie energetiche sostenibili.
• I tuoi compiti L'obiettivo di questo progetto PhD è quello di indagare le batterie allo stato solido a base di litio e di sodio utilizzando le tecniche di caratterizzazione di massa e interfaccia a base di muon. L'obiettivo principale è quello di ottenere una comprensione meccanicistica delle prestazioni elettrochimiche, con un focus sui processi di distribuzione, trasporto e degrado dell'ione durante il funzionamento della batteria. Il progetto affronta questioni chiave come la formazione di gradienti di concentrazione di Li/Na durante la carica e lo scarico, l'evoluzione delle interfase e dei meccanismi di degrado tra cui l'invecchiamento, la dissoluzione dei materiali (leaching), e la migrazione dei metalli di transizione. I metodi a base di muon saranno utilizzati per sondare le proprietà recuperate in profondità che sono difficili da accedere con le tecniche convenzionali, consentendo nuove intuizioni nelle interfacce sepolte e nei fenomeni di trasporto in massa. Il vostro lavoro si concentrerà sulla caratterizzazione elettrochimica e strutturale dei materiali e delle cellule della batteria, combinati con esperimenti basati su muon. Progetterai e eseguirai esperimenti per identificare le vie di reazione e i meccanismi di degradazione, e analizzerai set di dati complessi per collegare processi microscopici con prestazioni macroscopiche. Una stretta collaborazione con i partner del progetto sosterrà lo sviluppo e la sperimentazione di materiali e concetti cellulari. Il tuo profilo Hai un Master in chimica, scienza dei materiali, o un campo correlato, l'esperienza in elettrochimica o batterie è un vantaggio. Sono richieste eccellenti competenze in inglese. La nostra offerta Condurrai la tua ricerca nei laboratori di Empa a Dübendorf e sarai iscritto al programma di dottorato in Ingegneria Elettrica presso ETH Zurich. Il progetto fa parte del National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Muoniverse ed è finanziato dalla Swiss National Science Foundation. Muoniverse collega oltre 30 gruppi di ricerca e offre una scuola di ricerca strutturata con formazione, opportunità di scambio e sviluppo di carriera. Siamo alla ricerca di candidati che amano la ricerca collaborativa, interdisciplinare e l'apertura del valore e il progresso condiviso. Muoniverse si impegna a pari opportunità, diversità e una cultura della ricerca inclusiva. Potrai condurre in modo indipendente esperimenti, tra cui studi di teletrasporto, collaborare con partner accademici e industriali, e diffondere i risultati attraverso pubblicazioni e presentazioni. I nostri laboratori forniscono l'accesso a un'ampia gamma di infrastrutture di ricerca della batteria, tra cui glovebox, forni, spettroscopia, microscopia e vasti impianti di test elettrochimici. La data di inizio è il 1 ottobre 2026 o su accordo. Empa si impegna per la diversità, l'equità e l'inclusione. Noi incoraggiamo fortemente le applicazioni da ricercatori e individui di sesso femminile da backgrounds sottorappresentati. Crediamo che la diversità spinga l'innovazione e l'eccellenza scientifica. Unisciti a noi per contribuire alla ricerca innovativa nelle tecnologie energetiche sostenibili! Non vediamo l'ora di ricevere la vostra domanda online, tra cui una lettera di motivazione di due pagine, CV, record accademici, diplomi con trascrizioni, e almeno due lettere di riferimento. Saranno considerate solo le applicazioni complete. Si prega di caricare tutti i documenti attraverso la nostra pagina web, le applicazioni via E-mail non possono essere accettate.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Materialwissenschaft und Technologie sind unsere Leidenschaft. Mit unserer Spitzenforschung leisten die rund 1.100 Mitarbeiter der Empa wesentliche Beiträge zum Wohl der Gesellschaft für eine lebenswerte Zukunft. Die Empa ist eine Forschungseinrichtung des ETH-Bereichs. PhD-Position zu All-Solid-State-Batterien Der Fokus der Empa Labormaterialien für Energieumwandlung liegt auf Material- und Geräteinnovationen für nachhaltige Energietechnologien.
• Ihre Aufgaben Ziel dieses PhD-Projekts ist es, Lithium- und Natrium-basierte Festkörperbatterien unter Verwendung von Myonen-basierten Bulk- und Interface-Charakterisierungstechniken zu untersuchen. Hauptziel ist es, ein mechanistisches Verständnis der elektrochemischen Leistung zu erlangen, wobei der Schwerpunkt auf Ionenverteilung, -transport und -abbauprozessen während des Batteriebetriebs liegt. Das Projekt befasst sich mit Schlüsselfragen wie der Bildung von Li/Na-Konzentrationsgradienten während Ladung und Entladung, der Entwicklung von Interphasen und Abbaumechanismen einschließlich Alterung, Materialauflösung (Auslaugung) und Übergangsmetallmigration. Muon-basierte Methoden werden verwendet, um tief aufgelöste Eigenschaften zu untersuchen, die mit herkömmlichen Techniken schwer zugänglich sind, was neue Einblicke in vergrabene Schnittstellen und Massentransportphänomene ermöglicht. Ihre Arbeit konzentriert sich auf die elektrochemische und strukturelle Charakterisierung von Batteriematerialien und -zellen, kombiniert mit myonenbasierten Experimenten. Sie entwerfen und führen Experimente durch, um Reaktionswege und Abbaumechanismen zu identifizieren, und analysieren komplexe Datensätze, um mikroskopische Prozesse mit makroskopischer Leistung zu verbinden. Eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit den Projektpartnern wird die Entwicklung und Erprobung von Materialien und Zellkonzepten unterstützen. Dein Profil Sie haben einen Master-Abschluss in Chemie, Materialwissenschaften oder einem verwandten Bereich, Erfahrung in der Elektrochemie oder Batterien ist ein Vorteil. Hervorragende Englischkenntnisse sind erforderlich. Unser Angebot Sie forschen in den Empa-Laboratorien in Dübendorf und werden im Promotionsprogramm Elektrotechnik an der ETH Zürich eingeschrieben. Das Projekt ist Teil des National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) Muoniverse und wird vom Schweizerischen Nationalfonds gefördert. Muoniverse verbindet über 30 Forschungsgruppen und bietet eine strukturierte Forschungsschule mit Ausbildung, Austauschmöglichkeiten und Karriereentwicklung. Wir suchen Kandidaten, die kooperative, interdisziplinäre Forschung genießen und Wert auf Offenheit und gemeinsamen Fortschritt legen. Muoniverse setzt sich für Chancengleichheit, Vielfalt und eine inklusive Forschungskultur ein. Sie werden unabhängig Experimente durchführen, einschließlich Myon Beamline-Studien, mit akademischen und industriellen Partnern zusammenarbeiten und Ihre Ergebnisse durch Publikationen und Präsentationen verbreiten. Unsere Labore bieten Zugang zu einer breiten Palette von Batterieforschungsinfrastrukturen, darunter Gloveboxen, Öfen, Spektroskopie, Mikroskopie und umfangreiche elektrochemische Prüfeinrichtungen. Startdatum ist der 1. Oktober 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung. Die Empa setzt sich für Diversität, Gerechtigkeit und Inklusion ein. Wir empfehlen nachdrücklich Bewerbungen von Forscherinnen und Einzelpersonen mit unterrepräsentiertem Hintergrund. Wir glauben, dass Vielfalt Innovation und wissenschaftliche Exzellenz vorantreibt. Tragen Sie mit uns zu einer bahnbrechenden Forschung im Bereich nachhaltiger Energietechnologien bei! Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Online-Bewerbung mit einem zweiseitigen Motivationsschreiben, Lebenslauf, wissenschaftlichen Aufzeichnungen, Diplomen mit Transkripten und mindestens zwei Referenzschreiben. Es werden nur vollständige Anträge berücksichtigt. Bitte laden Sie alle Dokumente über unsere Webseite hoch, Bewerbungen per E-Mail können nicht angenommen werden.
descriptionByLocale.fr:
La science et la technologie des matériaux sont notre passion. Grâce à nos recherches de pointe, les quelque 1 100 employés d'Empa apportent une contribution essentielle au bien-être de la société pour un avenir digne d'être vécu. Empa est une institution de recherche du domaine ETH. Position du doctorat sur les piles à l'état solide Les matériaux de laboratoire pour la conversion de l'énergie sont axés sur l'innovation des matériaux et des appareils pour les technologies énergétiques durables.
• Vos tâches Le but de ce projet de doctorat est d'étudier les batteries solides à base de lithium et de sodium à l'aide de techniques de caractérisation en vrac et d'interface à base de muon. L'objectif principal est d'acquérir une compréhension mécaniste de la performance électrochimique, en mettant l'accent sur la distribution des ions, le transport et les processus de dégradation pendant le fonctionnement de la batterie. Le projet aborde des questions clés telles que la formation de gradients de concentration de Li/Na pendant la charge et la décharge, l'évolution des interphases et les mécanismes de dégradation, y compris le vieillissement, la dissolution des matériaux (délavage) et la migration des métaux de transition. Des méthodes basées sur le muon seront utilisées pour sonder les propriétés résolues en profondeur qui sont difficiles d'accès avec les techniques conventionnelles, ce qui permettra de découvrir de nouvelles interfaces enfouies et des phénomènes de transport en vrac. Votre travail se concentrera sur la caractérisation électrochimique et structurale des matériaux et des cellules des batteries, combinée à des expériences basées sur le muon. Vous concevrez et réaliserez des expériences pour identifier les voies de réaction et les mécanismes de dégradation, et analyserez des ensembles de données complexes pour relier les processus microscopiques aux performances macroscopiques. Une collaboration étroite avec les partenaires du projet appuiera l'élaboration et l'essai de matériaux et de concepts cellulaires.
• Votre profil Vous êtes titulaire d'un Master en chimie, science des matériaux, ou un domaine connexe, expérience en électrochimie ou batteries est un avantage. D'excellentes compétences en anglais sont requises. Notre offre Vous effectuerez vos recherches dans les laboratoires d'Empa à Dübendorf et vous serez inscrit au programme de doctorat en génie électrique à l'ETH Zurich. Le projet fait partie du Centre national de compétence en recherche (NCCR) Muoniverse et est financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences. Muoniverse relie plus de 30 groupes de recherche et offre une école de recherche structurée avec la formation, les possibilités d'échange et le développement de carrière. Nous recherchons des candidats qui aiment la recherche collaborative et interdisciplinaire et qui valorisent l'ouverture et le progrès partagé. Muoniverse est attachée à l'égalité des chances, à la diversité et à une culture de recherche inclusive. Vous effectuerez des expériences indépendantes, y compris des études de faisceaux muon, collaborerez avec des partenaires universitaires et industriels, et diffuserez vos résultats au moyen de publications et de présentations. Nos laboratoires offrent un large éventail d'infrastructures de recherche sur les piles, notamment des boîtes à gants, des fours, de la spectroscopie, de la microscopie et de vastes installations d'essais électrochimiques. La date de début est le 1er octobre 2026 ou sur accord. Empa est attachée à la diversité, à l'équité et à l'inclusion. Nous encourageons vivement les candidatures de femmes chercheurs et de personnes issues de milieux sous-représentés. Nous croyons que la diversité stimule l'innovation et l'excellence scientifique. Rejoignez-nous pour contribuer à la recherche révolutionnaire sur les technologies énergétiques durables! Nous sommes impatients de recevoir votre candidature en ligne, y compris une lettre de motivation de deux pages, un CV, des documents scientifiques, des diplômes avec transcriptions et au moins deux lettres de référence. Seules les demandes complètes seront examinées. Veuillez télécharger tous les documents via notre page Web, les applications par e-mail ne peuvent pas être acceptées.

jobs.title: Postdoc position: Chemist for selective ion scavenging in batteries

titleByLocale.it: Posizione Postdoc: Chemist per l'ion scavenging selettivo in batterie
titleByLocale.en: Postdoc position: Chemist for selective ion scavenging in batteries
titleByLocale.de: Postdoc-Position: Chemiker für selektive Ionenabscheidung in Batterien
titleByLocale.fr: Position postdoc: Chimiste pour la récupération sélective d'ions dans les batteries

jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

Postdoc position: Chemist for selective ion scavenging in batteries

Our Laboratory for Advanced Fibers in St. Gallen develops functional polymer fibers with applications in energy storage, health and environmental technologies. We are pioneering a new class of melt-spun liquid-core fibers that selectively scavenge transition metal ions and other degradation products in lithium-ion batteries, mitigating cell damage and prolonging battery life.

Your tasks

• Develop melt-spun liquid/gel-core fibers with polyolefin sheaths and functionalized, hydrophobic cores

• Explore selective scavenger systems for transition metal (TM) ions and HF, including chelating ligands, reactive nanoparticles and additives

• Optimize melt-spinning, uniaxial stretching, and post-treatment steps to control sheath porosity and ion diffusion

• Acquisition of research grants and writing of scientific publications

• Supervision of students and interns

• Collaborate closely with chemists, materials scientists, and electrochemists.

Your profile

• PhD in chemistry (or a closely related field such as polymer science or materials science)

• Experience with polymer–ion interactions, chelation chemistry, or battery materials is an advantage

• You enjoy interdisciplinary teamwork and are motivated to publish high-impact results

• Fluency in English; German is an asset.

Our offer

We offer an international, highly stimulating research environment with excellent infrastructure for fiber processing, polymer analysis, and electrochemical testing. You will be working at Empa in St. Gallen. The starting date is as soon as possible or upon mutual agreement, and the employment contract is limited to two years.

We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

descriptionByLocale.it:
La scienza dei materiali e la tecnologia sono la nostra passione. Con la nostra ricerca all'avanguardia, i circa 1.100 dipendenti di Empa danno un contributo essenziale al benessere della società per un futuro che vale la pena di vivere. Empa è un'istituzione di ricerca del dominio ETH.

Posizione Postdoc: Chemist per l'ion scavenging selettivo in batterie

Il nostro Laboratorio per Fibre Avanzate a St. Gallen sviluppa fibre polimeriche funzionali con applicazioni in stoccaggio energetico, salute e tecnologie ambientali. Siamo pionieri di una nuova classe di fibre liquide-core di fusione-spun che selettivamente scavenge ioni metallici di transizione e altri prodotti di degrado nelle batterie agli ioni di litio, mitigando i danni cellulari e prolungando la durata della batteria.

I tuoi compiti

• Sviluppare fibre liquide/gel-core con guaine in poliolefine e nucleo idrofobico funzionalizzato

• Esplorare sistemi di scavenger selettivi per ioni metallici di transizione (TM) e HF, compresi i leganti chelating, nanoparticelle reattive e additivi

• Ottimizzare le fasi di stretching, di stretching non assiale e post-trattamento per controllare la porosità della guaina e la diffusione di ioni

• Acquisizione di borse di ricerca e scrittura di pubblicazioni scientifiche

• Supervisione di studenti e tirocinanti

Il tuo profilo

jobs.description:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.

PhD position “Soft Active Matter Microrobots for Medicine (SAM3)”

Research project on Design, synthesis, and multiscale characterization of materials for soft robotics applications (SAM3/ESR12 – soft robotics)
 This project takes place within the Marie Curie Doctoral Network on Soft Active Matter Microrobots for Medicine (SAM3). This doctoral network of 12 PhD candidates aims at exploring the ear-nose-throat area from a microrobotics perspective. Thanks to active matter and small scale microrobotics engineering, three specific goals are targeted: (1) access the middle ear through the Eustachian tube; (2) access the olfactory clefts for mucosal biopsy; (3) access the skull cavity through the nose and the cribble plate for cerebrospinal fluid biopsy.

Your tasks

This specific PhD project will focus on design, synthesis, and multiscale characterization of materials for soft robotics applications and has application in all three endoscopic areas. The goal of the PhD is to computationally design using a simulation-guided approach and synthesize via light-based 3D-printing architecture (meta)materials for medical soft robotics applications. Furthermore, the morphology, microstructure, and mechanical behaviour of the metamaterials for soft robotics applications will be characterized as a function of environmental and boundary conditions in order to identify structureproperty- function relationships.
 The expected results are further set as follows: 1) Functional architectured material designs and synthesis routes via 3D printing with applications in medical soft robotic applications. 2) Characterization setup for probing mechanical behaviour of active and passive materials for soft robotics applications under various boundary conditions (variable strain rate, relative humidity, etc.). 3) Multiscale characterization of materials and systems developed in the SAM3 project in terms of process-structure-mechanical property-function relationships.

The candidate will be enrolled as PhD student at the Doctoral School for Materials Science and Engineering (EDMX) of EPFL (Lausanne, Switzerland) under co-supervision with Dr. Jakob Schwiedrzik and Prof. Dr. Johann MICHLER at EPFL and Empa (Thun, Switzerland) and will be based at the Laboratory for High Performance Ceramics of Empa (Dübendorf, Switzerland).

An academic stay of 3 months is planned at ULB (Prof Pierre LAMBERT, Bruxelles, Belgium) for the design of metamaterials for soft robotics, a second academic stay of 3 months is planned at UMONS (Prof Jérémy ODENT, Mons, Belgium) for the synthesis of soft robotics materials and an industrial secondment of 5 months is planned at Alemnis AG (Dr Jean-Marc BREGUET, Thun, Switzerland) for micromechanical testing of metamaterial structures.

Research environment

The PhD student will be jointly supervised by Dr Jakob SCHWIEDRZIK (Empa, Dübendorf, Switzerland) and Prof. Johann MICHLER (EPFL and Empa, Thun, Switzerland).

Posizione del dottorato “Soft Active Matter Microrobots for Medicine (SAM3)”

Progetto di ricerca su Design, sintesi e caratterizzazione multiscala di materiali per applicazioni robotiche morbide (SAM3/ESR12 – robotica morbida)
Questo progetto si svolge all'interno della Marie Curie Doctoral Network su Soft Active Matter Microrobots for Medicine (SAM3). Questa rete di dottorato di 12 candidati PhD mira a esplorare l'area del naso-torno auricolare da una prospettiva microrobotica. Grazie alla materia attiva e all'ingegneria microrobotica di piccola scala, tre obiettivi specifici sono presi di mira: (1) accedere all'orecchio medio attraverso il tubo eucaristico; (2) accedere alle fessure olfattive per la biopsia mucosa; (3) accedere alla cavità del cranio attraverso il naso e la piastra cribble per la biopsia del fluido cerebrospinale.

I tuoi compiti

Questo specifico progetto PhD si concentrerà sulla progettazione, la sintesi e la caratterizzazione multiscale di materiali per applicazioni robotiche morbide e ha applicazione in tutte e tre le aree endoscopiche. L'obiettivo del PhD è quello di progettare computazionalmente utilizzando un approccio guidato dalla simulazione e sintetizzare attraverso l'architettura 3D-printing basata sulla luce (meta) materiali per applicazioni medicali soft robotics. Inoltre, la morfologia, la microstruttura e il comportamento meccanico dei metamateriali per applicazioni robotiche morbide saranno caratterizzati da una funzione di condizioni ambientali e di confine al fine di identificare le relazioni strutturaproperty-funzionali.
I risultati attesi sono ulteriormente impostati come segue: 1) disegni e percorsi di sintesi di materiali architettonici funzionali tramite stampa 3D con applicazioni in applicazioni medicali soft robotic. 2) Configurazione di caratterizzazione per l'accertamento di comportamenti meccanici di materiali attivi e passivi per applicazioni robotiche morbide in varie condizioni di confine (variabile tasso di deformazione, umidità relativa, ecc.). 3) Caratterizzazione multiscala di materiali e sistemi sviluppati nel progetto SAM3 in termini di relazioni di proprietà-funzione-struttura-meccanica di processo.

Il candidato sarà iscritto come Dottorato di Ricerca presso la Scuola Medica per la Scienza e l'Ingegneria dei Materiali (EDMX) di EPFL (Lausanne, Svizzera) sotto la co-supervisione con Dr. Jakob Schwiedrzik e Prof. Il Dr. Johann MICHLER presso EPFL e Empa (Thun, Svizzera) e si baserà presso il Laboratorio di Ceramiche ad alte prestazioni di Empa (Dübendorf, Svizzera).

Un soggiorno accademico di 3 mesi è previsto presso ULB (Prof Pierre LAMBERT, Bruxelles, Belgio) per la progettazione di metamateriali per la robotica morbida, un secondo soggiorno accademico di 3 mesi è previsto presso UMONS (Prof Jérémy ODENT, Mons, Belgio) per la sintesi di materiali robotici morbidi e un distacco industriale di 5 mesi è previsto presso Alemnis AG (Dr Jean-Marc BREGUET, Thunechanical).

Ambiente di ricerca
Il principale laboratorio di ricerca sarà il Laboratorio di Ceramica ad alte prestazioni di Empa Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology (Dübendorf, Svizzera). Lo studente del dottorato sarà coadiuvato dal Dr. Jakob SCHWIEDRZIK (Empa, Dübendorf, Svizzera) e dal Prof. Johann MICHLER (EPFL e Empa, Thun, Svizzera).

Il Laboratorio per la Ceramica ad alte prestazioni di Empa è dotato di tutti i servizi necessari (installazioni e software di simulazione, laboratori chimici, DLP e 2 fotoni di stampa 3D, spettroscopia Raman, microscopia elettronica, nanoindentazione, test meccanici macroscopici, controllo dell'umidità) per la progettazione, produzione e caratterizzazione metamateriale. Il laboratorio è situato presso il campus principale di Empa a Dübendorf vicino alla città di Zurigo.

Il tuo profilo

• Nomineremo 1 PhD studente su questo progetto, relativo a 11 altre posizioni aperte nella rete SAM3 UE.

• Sarà iscritto all'interno della Scuola di Dottorato in Scienze e Ingegneria dei Materiali presso EPFL (Lausanne, Svizzera) con il Prof. Johann Michler e il dottor Jakob Schwiedrzik come supervisori.

• Il candidato deve avere una laurea magistrale o un diploma in scienze dei materiali, ingegneria meccanica, o simile, meno di 5 anni di carriera alla data di reclutamento e non avendo una laurea.

• Stiamo cercando studenti di talento e entusiasti di eseguire un dottorato, con un solido background in meccanica di materiali e simulazioni. L'esperienza con la caratterizzazione del materiale utilizzando la microscopia elettronica, la nanoindentazione, o altri metodi, e la stampa 3D basata sulla luce è un vantaggio.

• Per quanto riguarda le competenze morbide, il candidato dovrebbe avere una forte motivazione per la ricerca (curiosità, impegno, spirito di lavoro di squadra e aperto a discussioni con colleghi, scienza, modellazione, esperimenti, scrittura e capacità di comunicazione).

• Il candidato dovrebbe avere un buon comando di inglese parlato e scritto, e le competenze tedesche o francesi sono naturalmente un bene.

Per ulteriori informazioni sugli studi di dottorato presso l'EMPA, consultare il sito web (https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/edmx-materials-science-and-engineering/ ).

Data di inizio: Da ottobre 2026
Termine ultimo per la presentazione delle domande: 31 agosto 2026 anche se la posizione rimarrà aperta fino a quando non sarà riempita

Viviamo una cultura di inclusione e rispetto. Diamo il benvenuto a tutte le persone che sono interessate a attività innovative, sostenibili e significative - questo è ciò che conta.

Le domande devono essere inviate alla casella di posta SAM3@umons.ac.be dedicata solo al reclutamento. PhD Position "Soft Active Matter Microrobots für die Medizin (SAM3)"

Forschungsprojekt zu Design, Synthese und Multiskalencharakterisierung von Materialien für Soft Robotics Anwendungen (SAM3/ESR12 – Soft Robotics)
Dieses Projekt findet im Rahmen des Marie Curie Doctoral Network on Soft Active Matter Microrobots for Medicine (SAM3) statt. Dieses Doktorandennetzwerk von 12 PhD-Kandidaten zielt darauf ab, den Bereich Ohr-Nase-Nase aus einer Mikrorobotik-Perspektive zu erkunden. Dank der aktiven Materie und der Mikrorobotik im kleinen Maßstab werden drei spezifische Ziele angestrebt: (1) Zugang zum Mittelohr durch die Eustachische Röhre; (2) Zugang zu den olfaktorischen Spalten für die Schleimhautbiopsie; (3) Zugang zur Schädelhöhle durch die Nase und die Krippe für die Biopsie von Liquor cerebrospinal.

Ihre Aufgaben

Dieses spezifische PhD-Projekt wird sich auf Design, Synthese und Multiskalencharakterisierung von Materialien für weiche Robotikanwendungen konzentrieren und findet Anwendung in allen drei endoskopischen Bereichen. Das Ziel der Promotion ist es, rechnerisch mit einem simulationsgeführten Ansatz zu entwerfen und über lichtbasierte 3D-Druck-Architektur (Meta) Materialien für medizinische Soft Robotik-Anwendungen zu synthetisieren. Darüber hinaus werden Morphologie, Mikrostruktur und mechanisches Verhalten der Metamaterialien für weiche Robotikanwendungen in Abhängigkeit von Umwelt- und Randbedingungen charakterisiert, um Struktur-Eigenschafts-Funktionsbeziehungen zu identifizieren.
Die erwarteten Ergebnisse werden wie folgt festgelegt: 1 Funktional architektonische Materialdesigns und Synthesewege über 3D-Druck mit Anwendungen in medizinischen Soft Robot-Anwendungen. 2 Charakterisierungsaufbau zur Sondierung des mechanischen Verhaltens von aktiven und passiven Materialien für weiche Robotikanwendungen unter verschiedenen Randbedingungen (variable Dehnungsrate, relative Luftfeuchtigkeit usw.). 3) Multiskalige Charakterisierung von Materialien und Systemen, die im Projekt SAM3 im Hinblick auf Prozess-Struktur-mechanische Eigenschafts-Funktions-Beziehungen entwickelt wurden.

Der Kandidat wird als Doktorand an der Doktorandenschule für Materialwissenschaften und Ingenieurwissenschaften (EDMX) der EPFL (Lausanne, Schweiz) unter Co-Supervision mit Dr. Jakob Schwiedrzik und Prof. Dr. Schwiedrzik eingeschrieben. Dr. Johann MICHLER von der EPFL und der Empa (Thun, Schweiz) und wird am Labor für Hochleistungskeramik der Empa (Dübendorf, Schweiz) arbeiten.

Geplant ist ein akademischer Aufenthalt von 3 Monaten an der ULB (Prof Pierre LAMBERT, Bruxelles, Belgien) für die Gestaltung von Metamaterialien für die weiche Robotik, ein zweiter akademischer Aufenthalt von 3 Monaten an der UMONS (Prof Jérémy ODENT, Mons, Belgien) für die Synthese von weichen Robotikmaterialien und eine industrielle Entsendung von 5 Monaten an der Alemnis AG (Dr. Jean-Marc BREGUET, Thun, Schweiz) für die mikromechanische Prüfung von Metamaterialstrukturen.

Forschungsumgebung
Hauptforschungslabor wird das Labor für Hochleistungskeramik der Empa Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology (Dübendorf, Schweiz) sein. Der Doktorand wird gemeinsam betreut von Dr. Jakob SCHWIEDRZIK (Empa, Dübendorf, Schweiz) und Prof. Johann MICHLER (EPFL und Empa, Thun, Schweiz).

La science et la technologie des matériaux sont notre passion. Grâce à nos recherches de pointe, les quelque 1 100 employés d'Empa apportent une contribution essentielle au bien-être de la société pour un avenir digne d'être vécu. Empa est une institution de recherche du domaine ETH.

Poste de PhD : Microrobots pour la médecine (SAM3)

Projet de recherche sur la conception, la synthèse et la caractérisation à plusieurs échelles des matériaux pour les applications de robotique douce (SAM3/ESR12 – robotique douce)
Ce projet se déroule dans le cadre du Réseau doctoral Marie Curie sur les microrobots de matière active douce pour la médecine (SAM3). Ce réseau de doctorat de 12 doctorants vise à explorer la région de la gorge des oreilles dans une perspective microrobotique. Grâce à la matière active et à l'ingénierie microrobotique à petite échelle, trois objectifs spécifiques sont visés : (1) accéder à l'oreille moyenne par le tube d'Eustachian; (2) accéder aux fentes olfactives pour la biopsie muqueuse; (3) accéder à la cavité du crâne par le nez et à la plaque de graissage pour la biopsie du liquide céphalo-rachidien.

Vos tâches

Ce projet spécifique de doctorat se concentrera sur la conception, la synthèse et la caractérisation à plusieurs échelles des matériaux pour les applications robotiques douces et a une application dans les trois domaines endoscopiques. L'objectif du doctorat est de concevoir par calcul à l'aide d'une approche guidée par simulation et de synthétiser à l'aide d'architectures d'impression 3D (meta) basées sur la lumière pour les applications médicales de robotique douce. De plus, la morphologie, la microstructure et le comportement mécanique des métamatériaux pour les applications robotiques douces seront caractérisés en fonction des conditions environnementales et limites afin d'identifier les relations structure-fonction.
Les résultats attendus sont en outre définis comme suit : 1) Conceptions fonctionnelles de matériaux et voies de synthèse via l'impression 3D avec applications dans les applications robotiques médicales douces. 2) Configuration de caractérisation pour l'étude du comportement mécanique des matériaux actifs et passifs pour les applications robotiques douces dans diverses conditions limites (vitesse variable, humidité relative, etc.). 3) Caractérisation à plusieurs échelles des matériaux et des systèmes développés dans le cadre du projet SAM3 en termes de relations processus-structure-fonction mécanique.

Le candidat sera inscrit comme doctorant à l'Ecole Doctorale en Sciences des Matériaux et Ingénierie (EDMX) de l'EPFL (Lausanne, Suisse) sous co-supervision avec le Dr Jakob Schwiedrzik et le Prof. Dr. Johann MICHLER à l'EPFL et à Empa (Thun, Suisse) et sera basé au Laboratoire de Céramique haute performance d'Empa (Dübendorf, Suisse).

Un séjour académique de 3 mois est prévu à l'ULB (Prof Pierre LAMBERT, Bruxelles, Belgique) pour la conception de métamatériaux pour la robotique douce, un deuxième séjour académique de 3 mois est prévu à l'UMONS (Prof Jérémy ODENT, Mons, Belgique) pour la synthèse de matériaux de robotique douce et un détachement industriel de 5 mois est prévu à l'Alemnis AG (Dr Jean-Marc BREGUET, Thun, Suisse) pour les essais micromécaniques de structures métamatériaux.

Environnement de la recherche
Le principal laboratoire de recherche sera le Laboratoire de céramique haute performance des Laboratoires fédéraux de science et technologie des matériaux d'Empa (Dübendorf, Suisse). Le doctorant sera dirigé conjointement par le Dr Jakob SCHWIEDRZIK (Empa, Dübendorf, Suisse) et le Prof. Johann MICHLER (EPFL et Empa, Thoun, Suisse).

Le Laboratoire de Céramique Haute Performance d'Empa est équipé de toutes les installations nécessaires (stations et logiciels de simulation, laboratoires chimiques, DLP et 2 Photon Lithographie 3D, spectroscopie Raman, microscopie électronique, nano-identification, essais mécaniques macroscopiques, contrôle de l'humidité) pour la conception, la fabrication et la caractérisation des métamatériaux. Le laboratoire est situé sur le campus principal d'Empa à Dübendorf près de la ville de Zürich.

Votre profil

• Nous nommerons 1 doctorant sur ce projet, lié à 11 autres postes ouverts dans le réseau SAM3.

• Il/elle sera inscrit(e) à l'Ecole Doctorale en Sciences des Matériaux et Ingénierie de l'EPFL (Lausanne, Suisse) auprès du Prof. Johann Michler et le Dr Jakob Schwiedrzik en tant que superviseurs.

• Le candidat doit avoir une maîtrise ou un diplôme en sciences des matériaux, en génie mécanique ou similaire, moins de 5 ans de carrière à la date de recrutement et ne pas avoir de doctorat.

• Nous recherchons des étudiants talentueux et enthousiastes pour effectuer un doctorat, avec une solide expérience en mécanique des matériaux et des simulations. L'expérience de la caractérisation des matériaux à l'aide de la microscopie électronique, de la nano-identification ou d'autres méthodes, et de l'impression 3D basée sur la lumière est un avantage.

• En ce qui concerne les compétences douces, le candidat devrait avoir une forte motivation pour la recherche (curiosité, engagement, esprit d'équipe et ouverture aux discussions avec ses collègues, science, modélisation, expériences, compétences en écriture et en communication).
